title: U.S. County Demographic Explorer: ACS by County
description: Explore county demographics with the U.S. County Demographic Explorer — population, age, income and housing from Census and ACS data. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, Los Angeles County's 10,014,009 residents (2020 Census) make it more populous than most US states — while Loving County, Texas counted 64 people in the same census.
quick_answer: The U.S. County Demographic Explorer presents Census and American Community Survey data for America's 3,143 counties and county equivalents — population, age, income, housing and more — county by county. Pick a county and read its profile: official statistics, with their survey margins kept visible instead of averaged away.

Los Angeles County: 10,014,009 people (2020 Census) — more than 40 individual states. Loving County, Texas: 64 people, the nation's least populous county. One explorer holds both, and the ACS treats the second with the statistical caution its sample size demands.

body.t: An ACS median income of $58,000 ± $4,000 for a small county is not '$58,000'. The margin is the survey telling you its own resolution — the explorer shows it because hiding it would be a lie of precision.

popular_table.note: County counts: 3,143 counties and county equivalents (including Louisiana parishes, Alaska boroughs and independent cities) per the Census Bureau. ACS values are estimates from a survey, not counts — the explorer labels each figure's source and period.

faq: Why do two counties' data years differ?

Large counties publish ACS 1-year estimates; small ones appear only in 5-year pooled estimates. Comparing a 2023 1-year figure against a 2019–2023 5-year one is comparing different instruments — the profiles label each value's series and period.
What is a good use of the explorer?

Screening, learning and first-draft research: understanding a county's shape before deeper work. Regulated decisions (lending, insurance, eligibility) require the underlying official extracts and their full documentation.
The decennial backbone changes every ten years; ACS series republish annually. The explorer follows the Census Bureau's release cycle, with vintages named on the profiles.
Parishes (Louisiana), boroughs and census areas (Alaska), independent cities (Virginia and others), and the District of Columbia — 3,143 units total in the Bureau's county framework.
Can I see tracts instead of counties?
Tract-level ACS exists and is finer; the Census Geography Finder supplies tract IDs for any point. This explorer's grain is deliberately the county — America's administrative atom.
Why is a tiny county's income figure fuzzy?
ACS interviews a sample; in a county of 64 people the sample is a handful of households, and the published margin is correspondingly honest. Treat small-county point values as ranges.

County boundaries rarely change, so decennial comparisons are mostly clean — the exceptions (Alaska reorganisations, new Virginia independents) are footnoted by the Bureau and flagged in careful work.
